sections.html:
Bend is a Central Oregon city on the Deschutes River, east of the Cascade Range, and the seat of Deschutes County. It covers about 35 square miles at an elevation near 3,640 feet, with Pilot Butte, an extinct cinder cone, inside the city limits. The U.S. Forest Service owns about 51 percent of the land across Deschutes County.

The 2020 census counted 99,178 residents, up 29.4 percent from 76,639 in 2010, with an estimate of 106,926 for 2024. Housing tenure in 2020 was 60.6 percent owner-occupied and 39.4 percent renter-occupied, across 44,449 housing units. Deschutes County was formed on December 13, 1916, with Bend as its seat. The biggest employers are St. Charles Health System and the Bend-La Pine School District, and tourism and retirement help drive growth.

Bend has a cold semi-arid climate. It gets about 10.6 inches of precipitation and 21.6 inches of snow a year. January highs average 42.5 degrees and lows 24.6, while July highs average 83.8. The record low is minus 26, and freezing temperatures are possible from about mid-September to mid-June.

  • Frozen pipes and shallow water lines are a winter risk in vacant houses.
  • Roof snow load and ice dams matter for older roofs.
  • Dry summers raise wildfire concerns for houses near trees and the national forest.
  • Big day and night swings, up to 35 degrees in summer, stress paint, decks and exterior wood.

A house left empty over winter can develop plumbing damage quickly, and an inherited or second-home property is often vacant.

In Bend, wildfire risk shows up as insurance cost and availability. Oregon's legislature passed Senate Bill 83 in 2025 to repeal the state wildfire hazard map and its building code requirements. Before the repeal, Deschutes County had 21,258 lots classified as high hazard. A 2023 law had already barred insurers from using the map for pricing or coverage, yet Central Oregon owners still reported large premium increases and coverage cutbacks, since insurers use their own models.

The Oregon Division of Financial Regulation lists these defensible space steps:

  • Clear dry leaves, brush and pine needles from the yard and gutters.
  • Trim trees back from the structure.
  • Screen open vents.

If your house has fire-prone landscaping or a rough roof, an as-is sale lets the buyer decide how to handle it. The state's page on wildfire and insurance explains policyholder rights.

Bend requires a land use permit and an operating license for most short-term rentals, meaning stays of fewer than 30 consecutive days. Permits approved after April 15, 2015 end when the property sells.

  • Operating licenses are never transferable.
  • Permits approved on or before April 15, 2015 run with the land, and the new owner must apply for an operating license within 60 days of closing.
  • A City of Bend business registration is required.
  • Most rentals owe a 10.4 percent room tax on gross revenue.

A buyer of a vacation rental cannot assume the rental income will carry over. Call the City's Licensing office at 541-388-5580 extension 8, or planning at extension 3, before you promote the house as an income property. Current fees are listed on the city's short-term rental page.

sections.h2: Selling with a tenant in place
sections.html:
You can sell a Bend rental with the tenant staying, and with 39.4 percent of housing renter-occupied, many owners do. ORS 90.427 limits ending a tenancy for a sale. After the tenant's first year, a landlord needs an accepted offer from a buyer who will live in the home and must give at least 90 days of written notice.

The landlord also owes one month's rent when delivering that notice, unless the landlord owns four or fewer covered units. Breaking the rule can cost three months' rent plus damages, so a sale that keeps the lease in place is often the lower-risk route.

Deschutes County sends Bend property tax statements in October. The first installment and the full-pay discount fall in mid-November, with a 3 percent discount for paying in full and 2 percent for paying two thirds.

InstallmentWhen it is due
Full pay or first thirdMid-November (November 15, or the next business day)
Second thirdMid-February
Final installmentMay 15

The county's tax office is at 541-388-6540 or taxoffice@deschutes.org. If you sell mid-year, the escrow company prorates the bill between you and the buyer. Appeals to the county Board of Property Tax Appeals are due December 31.

sections.h2: Seller checklist for a Bend house
sections.html:
1. Find out whether the house is vacant. If it is, confirm the water is shut off or the heat is on, because freezing is possible from about mid-September to mid-June.
  2. Look at the yard, gutters and roof for pine needles, brush and dry leaves, since buyers and insurers ask about them.
  3. If the house has been a vacation rental, check the permit date and tell buyers plainly that operating licenses never transfer.
  4. If a tenant lives there, decide whether to sell with the lease in place, which avoids the 90-day notice and the month's rent owed with it.
  5. Request the tax balance from the county tax office at 541-388-6540 and give it to the title company.

Selling as-is means a buyer takes on whatever is on this list, so the paperwork matters more than the paint.

Bend takes its name from a bend in the Deschutes River that pioneers forded. It was platted in 1904 and incorporated in January 1905, and a dam built in 1910 created Mirror Pond. Lumber carried the early economy, and the Shevlin-Hixon Lumber mill closed in 1950. Today St. Charles Health System and the school district lead local hiring, which keeps demand from resting on a single employer.

Bend has 13 official neighborhood districts, including Awbrey Butte, Boyd Acres, Century West, Larkspur, Mountain View, Old Bend, Old Farm District, Orchard District, River West, Southeast Bend, Southern Crossing, Southwest Bend and Summit West.

US 20 and US 97 meet in Bend, and US 97 runs through the city as the Bend Parkway. Century Drive leads to the ski area southwest of town. Roberts Field in Redmond, 18 miles north, has direct flights to cities including Seattle, Denver, Los Angeles and San Francisco, and Cascades East Transit runs nine fixed bus routes from the Hawthorne Transit Center.

Whatever shape your house is in, the order of events is the same. You receive an offer, the title company searches the deed and any liens, and escrow prepares a settlement statement that splits the property tax between you and the buyer. A cash sale removes the lender appraisal, so a vacant house with winter plumbing damage, an inherited property or a rental with a tenant can close without repair demands. Ask your escrow officer for the proration and any payoff figures before you sign.

faqs.a: Yes. Bend is the county seat of Deschutes County, which was formed on December 13, 1916.

faqs.q: Does selling a Bend vacation rental transfer the short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: Not for newer permits. Permits approved after April 15, 2015 are tied to the owner and become void when the property sells, and operating licenses never transfer.

faqs.q: What is Bend's coldest recorded temperature?
faqs.a: The record low is minus 26 degrees, recorded in January and February.

faqs.q: When are Bend property taxes due?
faqs.a: In mid-November for full payment or the first third, mid-February for the second and May 15 for the last. A full payment earns 3 percent off, and dates move when November 15 lands on a weekend.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bend house with wildfire risk or old landscaping?
faqs.a: Yes. Oregon repealed its state wildfire hazard map in 2025, but insurers still price risk with their own models, so buyers should expect questions about defensible space.
